findings.message: The function splitNumberUnit returns an empty numeric prefix when the input string starts with a non-numeric character (e.g., "GB" or ".5GB"). This causes the caller to fail with a parse error or return 0, whereas standard size parsing should support implicit leading zeros ("GB" -> 1GB) and leading decimals (".5GB" -> 0.5GB).
findings.suggestion: Modify the loop to skip leading non-numeric characters (except '.') or handle the case where i == 0 by returning "0" as the numeric prefix.
